decls.name: TauCeti.pow_apply_eq_self_iff_of_isCycle
decls.doc:
A power of a cycle fixes a point of its support exactly when the exponent is a multiple of the
length of the cycle, in which case the power is the identity.

The right-hand side does not mention `x`: such a power either moves every point of the support or
moves none of them.
decls.statement:
theorem pow_apply_eq_self_iff_of_isCycle (hf : f.IsCycle) {x : α} (hx : x ∈ f.support) (k : ℕ) :
    (f ^ k) x = x ↔ f.support.card ∣ k

decls.name: TauCeti.pow_apply_ne_self_of_isCycle
decls.doc:
A power of a cycle moves every point of the support of that cycle, unless its exponent is a
multiple of the length of the cycle.
decls.statement:
theorem pow_apply_ne_self_of_isCycle (hf : f.IsCycle) {k : ℕ} (hk : ¬f.support.card ∣ k) {x : α}
    (hx : x ∈ f.support) : (f ^ k) x ≠ x

decls.name: TauCeti.card_support_of_mem_cycleFactorsFinset_pow
decls.doc:
Every cycle of a power of a cycle of length `n` has the same length, namely the order
`n / gcd n k` of that power.

decls.name: TauCeti.cycleType_pow_of_isCycle
decls.doc:
The cycle type of a power of a cycle: writing `n = f.support.card` for the length of the
cycle, the permutation `f ^ k` is a product of `gcd n k` disjoint cycles, each of length
`n / gcd n k`.

The exponent is assumed not to be a multiple of `n`, which is exactly what rules out
`f ^ k = 1`.
decls.statement:
theorem cycleType_pow_of_isCycle (hf : f.IsCycle) {k : ℕ} (hk : ¬f.support.card ∣ k) :
    (f ^ k).cycleType =
      Multiset.replicate (f.support.card.gcd k) (f.support.card / f.support.card.gcd k)

decls.name: TauCeti.fiberSubgroup
decls.doc:
The subgroup of permutations of `α` that preserve every fiber of `f : α → ι`, that is, those
moving each point within its own fiber.
decls.statement: def fiberSubgroup (f : α → ι) : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm α)

decls.name: TauCeti.mem_fiberSubgroup
decls.statement:
theorem mem_fiberSubgroup {f : α → ι} {σ : Equiv.Perm α} :
    σ ∈ fiberSubgroup f ↔ ∀ a, f (σ a) = f a

decls.name: TauCeti.swap_mem_fiberSubgroup
decls.doc:
The transposition of two points lying in a common fiber of `f` preserves every fiber of `f`:
it moves each of the two points to the other, inside their shared fiber, and fixes the rest.
decls.statement:
theorem swap_mem_fiberSubgroup [DecidableEq α] {f : α → ι} {x y : α} (h : f x = f y) :
    Equiv.swap x y ∈ fiberSubgroup f

decls.name: TauCeti.fiberSubgroup_map_conj
decls.doc:
Conjugation by `e` transports the subgroup preserving the fibers of `f` to the subgroup
preserving the fibers of `g` when `e` identifies their fiber equivalence relations.
decls.statement:
theorem fiberSubgroup_map_conj {f : α → ι} {g : α → κ} (e : Equiv.Perm α)
    (h : ∀ a b, f a = f b ↔ g (e a) = g (e b)) :
    (fiberSubgroup f).map (MulAut.conj e).toMonoidHom = fiberSubgroup g

decls.name: TauCeti.fiberSubgroup_inf
decls.doc: Preserving the fibers of two maps at once is preserving the fibers of the paired map.
decls.statement:
theorem fiberSubgroup_inf (f : α → ι) (g : α → κ) :
    fiberSubgroup f ⊓ fiberSubgroup g = fiberSubgroup fun a => (f a, g a)

decls.name: TauCeti.fiberSubgroup_eq_bot_of_injective
decls.doc: Only the identity preserves the fibers of an injective map, its fibers being singletons.
decls.statement:
theorem fiberSubgroup_eq_bot_of_injective {f : α → ι} (hf : Function.Injective f) :
    fiberSubgroup f = ⊥

decls.name: TauCeti.injective_of_fiberSubgroup_eq_bot
decls.doc:
If the identity is the only permutation preserving the fibers of `f`, then `f` is injective:
two points in a common fiber would be exchanged by a nontrivial fiber-preserving transposition.
decls.statement:
theorem injective_of_fiberSubgroup_eq_bot {f : α → ι}
    (h : fiberSubgroup f = ⊥) : Function.Injective f

decls.name: TauCeti.fiberSubgroup_eq_bot_iff
decls.doc: The fibers of `f` are preserved only by the identity exactly when `f` is injective.
decls.statement:
theorem fiberSubgroup_eq_bot_iff {f : α → ι} :
    fiberSubgroup f = ⊥ ↔ Function.Injective f

decls.name: TauCeti.fiberSubgroupMulEquivStabilizer
decls.doc:
The permutations preserving the fibers of `f` are the stabilizer of `f` for the domain action
of `Equiv.Perm α` on `α → ι`, read as a subgroup of `Equiv.Perm α` itself: the `ᵈᵐᵃ` and `ᵐᵒᵖ`
synonyms reverse multiplication twice, so `σ ↦ DomMulAct.mk σ` is an isomorphism.
decls.statement:
def fiberSubgroupMulEquivStabilizer (f : α → ι) :
    fiberSubgroup f ≃* (MulAction.stabilizer (Equiv.Perm α)ᵈᵐᵃ f)ᵐᵒᵖ

decls.name: TauCeti.fiberSubgroupMulEquivStabilizer_apply_unop_coe
decls.doc:
Read in `(Equiv.Perm α)ᵈᵐᵃ`, the stabilizer element attached to a fiber-preserving permutation
is that permutation.
decls.statement:
theorem fiberSubgroupMulEquivStabilizer_apply_unop_coe (f : α → ι) (σ : fiberSubgroup f) :
    ((fiberSubgroupMulEquivStabilizer f σ).unop : (Equiv.Perm α)ᵈᵐᵃ) =
      DomMulAct.mk (σ : Equiv.Perm α)

decls.name: TauCeti.fiberSubgroupMulEquivStabilizer_symm_apply_coe
decls.doc:
Read in `Equiv.Perm α`, the fiber-preserving permutation attached to an element of the
stabilizer is that element.
decls.statement:
theorem fiberSubgroupMulEquivStabilizer_symm_apply_coe (f : α → ι)
    (g : (MulAction.stabilizer (Equiv.Perm α)ᵈᵐᵃ f)ᵐᵒᵖ) :
    (((fiberSubgroupMulEquivStabilizer f).symm g : fiberSubgroup f) : Equiv.Perm α) =
      DomMulAct.mk.symm (g.unop : (Equiv.Perm α)ᵈᵐᵃ)

decls.name: TauCeti.fiberSubgroupMulEquivPiPerm
decls.doc:
Restricting a fiber-preserving permutation of `α` to each fiber of `f` is an isomorphism onto
the product of the permutation groups of the fibers.

This is Mathlib's `DomMulAct.stabilizerMulEquiv` transported along
`fiberSubgroupMulEquivStabilizer`.
decls.statement:
def fiberSubgroupMulEquivPiPerm (f : α → ι) :
    fiberSubgroup f ≃* ∀ i, Equiv.Perm {a // f a = i}

decls.name: TauCeti.fiberSubgroupMulEquivPiPerm_apply_coe
decls.statement:
theorem fiberSubgroupMulEquivPiPerm_apply_coe (f : α → ι) (σ : fiberSubgroup f) (i : ι)
    (a : {a // f a = i}) :
    (fiberSubgroupMulEquivPiPerm f σ i a : α) = (σ : Equiv.Perm α) a

decls.name: TauCeti.fiberSubgroupMulEquivPiPerm_symm_apply
decls.doc:
The fiber-preserving permutation assembled from a family of permutations of the fibers of `f`
moves each point by the permutation of its own fiber.
decls.statement:
theorem fiberSubgroupMulEquivPiPerm_symm_apply (f : α → ι)
    (σ : ∀ i, Equiv.Perm {a // f a = i}) (a : α) :
    ((fiberSubgroupMulEquivPiPerm f).symm σ : Equiv.Perm α) a = (σ (f a) ⟨a, rfl⟩ : α)

decls.name: TauCeti.fiberSubgroupMulEquivPiPerm_trans_piCongrRight_apply
decls.doc:
Reading `fiberSubgroupMulEquivPiPerm f` through equivalences `e i : {a // f a = i} ≃ β i` of
the fibers of `f`: the `i`-th component takes the point of `β i` matching `a` to the one matching
`σ a`.  Specialising this to a concrete family of fibers gives the component formula for the
transported isomorphism.
decls.statement:
theorem fiberSubgroupMulEquivPiPerm_trans_piCongrRight_apply (f : α → ι)
    (e : ∀ i, {a // f a = i} ≃ β i) (σ : fiberSubgroup f) (i : ι) (a : {a // f a = i}) :
    (fiberSubgroupMulEquivPiPerm f).trans
        (MulEquiv.piCongrRight fun i => (e i).permCongrHom) σ i (e i a) =
      e i ⟨(σ : Equiv.Perm α) a, (mem_fiberSubgroup.mp σ.2 a).trans a.2⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.fiberSubgroupMulEquivPiPerm_trans_piCongrRight_symm_apply
decls.doc:
Reading the inverse of `fiberSubgroupMulEquivPiPerm f` through equivalences
`e i : {a // f a = i} ≃ β i` of the fibers of `f`: the assembled permutation moves each point by
the permutation of its own fiber, read through `e`.
decls.statement:
theorem fiberSubgroupMulEquivPiPerm_trans_piCongrRight_symm_apply (f : α → ι)
    (e : ∀ i, {a // f a = i} ≃ β i) (σ : ∀ i, Equiv.Perm (β i)) (a : α) :
    ((((fiberSubgroupMulEquivPiPerm f).trans
        (MulEquiv.piCongrRight fun i => (e i).permCongrHom)).symm σ : Equiv.Perm α) a : α) =
      ((e (f a)).symm (σ (f a) (e (f a) ⟨a, rfl⟩)) : α)
